Fear a Day when all are returned to Allah and every soul is paid in full for what it earned, without injustice.
They affirm that Allah will gather the people for a Day about which there is no doubt, for Allah does not fail in His promise.
On the Day every soul finds its good and evil deeds before it, it will wish its evil were far away, and Allah is kind to His servants.
On the Day some faces turn white and some black: those who disbelieved after believing taste punishment, while the white-faced abide forever in Allah's mercy.
Allah does no injustice and multiplies good deeds; He will bring a witness from every nation, and that Day disbelievers will wish the earth covered them.
There is no deity except Allah, who will surely assemble all for the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt.
On the Day Allah assembles the messengers and asks their response, they will say they have no knowledge and that He knows the unseen.
On the Day of gathering, the jinn and their human allies who made use of each other will be told the Fire is their eternal residence.
Those sent messengers and the messengers themselves will be questioned, deeds will be related and weighed in truth: heavy scales bring success, light scales loss.
Asked when the Hour will come, the Prophet says its knowledge is only with Allah; it weighs on the heavens and earth and will come unexpectedly.
On the Day all are gathered, the 'partners' say they were unaware of being worshipped, and every soul is tried for its deeds and returned to Allah.
When gathered, they will feel they stayed an hour; each nation is judged justly when its messenger comes; deniers ask when the promise comes, and wrongdoers will taste eternal punishment.
A sign for those who fear the Hereafter's punishment: a witnessed Day when people are gathered, delayed only for a set term, when no soul speaks except by His permission.
All come out before Allah; the weak ask the arrogant to avail them against the punishment, and the arrogant say they have no escape, whether impatient or patient.
Allah delays the wrongdoers for a Day of staring eyes, when they will beg for respite; the earth and heavens are replaced, and criminals are shackled in garments of pitch.
On the Day a witness is raised from every nation, disbelievers get no excuse, the partners they invoked call them liars, and the Prophet is witness over his nation.
On the Day every soul will come disputing for itself, each will be fully repaid for what it did, and none will be wronged.
Each person's fate is fastened to his neck, and on Resurrection Day he reads his open record; no one bears another's burden, and Allah punishes none before sending a messenger.
On the Day every people is called with its record, those given it in the right hand read it unwronged, and whoever was blind here is blind in the Hereafter.
On the Day the mountains are moved, all are gathered and presented in rows, and the record is laid open, missing nothing small or great, and no one is wronged.
On the Day they are told to call the partners they claimed for Allah, none will answer, and the criminals will see the Fire with no way out.
On that day they surge over one another, the Horn is blown and all are gathered, and Hell is displayed, prepared as a lodging for disbelievers blind to His remembrance.
They will hear and see clearly on the Day they come to Allah; the heedless are warned of the Day of Regret, and all will return to Him.
On the Day the righteous are gathered to the Most Merciful as a delegation and the criminals driven thirsty to Hell, only those with a covenant from Him may intercede.
When the Horn is blown, criminals murmur that they stayed briefly, mountains are blown away, voices are hushed, only permitted intercession helps, and believers fear no injustice.
Allah sets the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection, so no soul is wronged, and even a mustard seed's weight is brought forth.
On that Day Allah will fold the heaven like a scroll of records and repeat creation as He began it, a promise binding on Him.
Mankind is told to fear their Lord, for the convulsion of the Hour is terrible: nursing mothers will be distracted, pregnant women will miscarry, and people will seem intoxicated.
Allah will judge on the Day of Resurrection between the believers, Jews, Sabeans, Christians, Magians and those who associate others with Him, for He witnesses all things.
Disbelievers stay in doubt until the Hour comes suddenly; that Day all sovereignty is Allah's, believers enter the Gardens of Pleasure and deniers of His signs face humiliating punishment.
When the Horn is blown no ties remain; those with heavy scales succeed, while those with light scales lose themselves in Hell, their faces seared by the Fire.
On the Day Allah gathers them with what they worshipped, the worshipped deny taking allies besides Him and say comforts made the worshippers forget the message.
Those not expecting to meet Allah demand to see angels; when they do, criminals get no good tidings, the heaven splits, and the wrongdoer regrets his friend.
On the Day deniers from every nation are gathered and the Horn is blown, all are terrified and mountains pass like clouds; good deeds bring better, evil deeds the Fire.
On the Day Allah asks for their claimed partners, the misleaders disown them, the partners do not answer, none can answer about the messengers, and the repentant believers succeed.
On the Day Allah asks for their claimed partners, a witness is taken from every nation, they are told to bring proof, and what they invented is lost.
When the Hour arrives the criminals will despair, their claimed partners will not intercede for them, and people will be separated.
When the Hour comes, criminals will swear they stayed only an hour, those given knowledge say they stayed as Allah decreed, and the wrongdoers' excuses will not help.
People are told to fear their Lord and a Day when no father or son can help the other, and not be deluded by worldly life or the Deceiver.
People ask the Prophet about the Hour; its knowledge is only with Allah, and perhaps it is near.
Disbelievers say the Hour will not come, but it will; the Knower of the unseen records every atom's weight to reward believers and punish those who strive against His verses.
Disbelievers ask when the promised Day comes; it is fixed, and there the oppressed and the arrogant who rejected the Quran will blame each other before their Lord.
When Allah gathers all and asks the angels whether these people worshipped them, the angels say it was the jinn, and the wrongdoers are told to taste the Fire.
On the Day of Resurrection no soul will carry another's burden, even a relative's; the Prophet can warn only those who fear their Lord unseen and establish prayer.
On that Day mouths will be sealed, and hands will speak and feet testify about what people earned.
On the Day of Recompense, wrongdoers and what they worshipped are led to the path of Hellfire and questioned; followers and misleaders blame each other, but all share the punishment.
On Resurrection Day liars about Allah will have blackened faces and Hell will house the arrogant, while Allah saves the God-fearing from evil and grief.
People have not valued Allah rightly; on Resurrection Day the earth is in His grip, the Horn is blown twice, records are placed, and all are judged justly.
Allah inspires whom He wills to warn of the Day of Meeting, when nothing is hidden, all sovereignty is His, every soul is recompensed and wrongdoers have no intercessor.
The Hour is certainly coming, without doubt, but most people do not believe.
The enemies of Allah gathered to the Fire find their hearing, eyes and skins testifying against them, ruined by assuming Allah did not know much of what they did.
Those arguing about Allah have invalid arguments; Allah sent down the Book and the balance, the Hour may be near, and disputers about it are in extreme error.
They await only the Hour coming suddenly, when close friends will become enemies to each other except the righteous.
The Day of Judgement is the appointed time for all, when no relative can help another, except those on whom Allah has mercy.
When the Hour comes every nation kneels, called to its record; believers enter Allah's mercy, while disbelievers who mocked His verses and doubted the Hour are left in the Fire.
They wait only for the Hour to come suddenly, though its indications have come, and remembrance will not help them then.
When the Horn is blown each soul comes with a driver and a witness; every obstinate disbeliever is thrown into Hell, his companion disowns him, and Allah wrongs no one.
By the scattering winds, laden clouds, sailing ships and apportioning angels, what you are promised is true and the recompense will occur.
By the mount, an inscribed Book, the frequented House, the raised heaven and the filled sea, your Lord's punishment will occur, on the Day the heaven sways and mountains depart.
The Prophet is a warner like those before; the Approaching Day has drawn near and none but Allah can remove it, so prostrate to Allah and worship Him.
Jinn and mankind will be attended to and cannot pass beyond heaven and earth without authority; flame and smoke will come, the heaven will split, and none asked about sin.
When the Occurrence comes it lowers some and raises others; the earth shakes, mountains crumble to dust, and people become three groups: right, left and forerunners.
On the Day of Assembly, the Day of Deprivation, believers who do righteousness enter gardens with misdeeds removed, while those who deny Allah's verses abide in the Fire.
Disbelievers ask when the promise will come; its knowledge is with Allah alone, and when they see it approaching their faces will be distressed.
On the Day the shin is uncovered, disbelievers called to prostrate will be unable, eyes humbled and disgraced, though they were called to it while sound.
The Inevitable Reality, a name for the Day of Judgement, is announced, and people are asked what can make them know what it is.
When the Horn blows once, earth and mountains are crushed, the heaven splits, angels stand at its edges, eight bear the Throne, and people are exhibited with nothing hidden.
A supplicant asked for the disbelievers' punishment on a Day of fifty thousand years, when the sky is like murky oil and the criminal would offer his family as ransom.
Disbelievers are asked how they will guard against a Day that turns children white-haired, when the heaven breaks apart, for Allah's promise is always fulfilled.
When the trumpet is blown, that Day will be hard and not easy for the disbelievers.
When sight is dazzled and the sun and moon are joined, man will seek escape but find none; he will be told his deeds and be a witness against himself.
People love the fleeting life and neglect the Hereafter; that Day some faces will be radiant, looking at their Lord, and others contorted, expecting a backbreaking blow.
By the winds and the message-bringing angels, what is promised will happen: stars are obliterated, the heaven opens, mountains are blown away, and woe that Day to the deniers.
On the Day of Judgement the deniers will not speak or be allowed excuses; all peoples are assembled, and they are challenged to plan against Allah if they can.
People question one another about the great news, the Day of Judgement, over which they disagree; they will soon come to know.
The Day of Judgement is appointed: the Horn is blown, people come in multitudes, the heaven opens into gateways and the mountains become a mirage.
On the True Day the Spirit and angels stand in rows, none speaking without permission; each will see what he sent ahead, and the disbeliever will wish he were dust.
By the angels who take souls and arrange affairs, on the Day of the blast and the one that follows, hearts will tremble and eyes be humbled.
They ask the Prophet when the Hour comes; its time rests with his Lord, he is only a warner, and they will feel they stayed but an afternoon or morning.
When the Deafening Blast comes, a man flees from his brother, parents, wife and children; some faces will be bright and joyful, others dark with dust, the disbelievers.
When the sun is darkened, stars fall, seas are aflame, the buried girl is asked why she was killed, Hellfire blazes and Paradise nears, each soul knows what it brought.
When the sky breaks apart, stars scatter, seas erupt and graves are overturned, each soul will know what it sent forth and kept back.
People deny the Recompense, though noble keepers are appointed over them, recording and knowing whatever they do.
The Day of Recompense is when no soul can do anything for another, and the command that Day is entirely Allah's.
When the sky splits and the earth is stretched out and casts out its contents, obeying its Lord, mankind is told it labors toward its Lord and will meet it.
When the earth is crushed, the Lord comes with angels in ranks and Hell is brought near, man will remember too late, wishing he had sent good ahead.
When the earth quakes, throws out its burdens and reports its news, people come forth in groups to see their deeds, every atom's weight of good or evil.
When the graves' contents are scattered and what is in the breasts is laid bare, their Lord will be fully acquainted with them that Day.
On the Day of the Striking Calamity people are like scattered moths and mountains like fluffed wool; heavy scales bring a pleasant life, light scales an intensely hot Fire.
